title: Aniimo Catching Guide | Every Aniipod Type, Catch Tips And Best Pods | Aniimo Guide
description: A full guide to catching in Aniimo: how throws work, stealth and back attack tips, weakening targets, and every Aniipod type from the standard pod to the Ultra and Sparkling Cube. Checked against several guides in October 2026; numbers can change with patches, so trust the catch chance shown in your game.

sections.heading: Why catching matters
sections.script: Catching is the heart of Aniimo. Every team you build starts with an Aniipod flying through the air, so learning how catching works saves you a lot of time and a lot of resources. In this video we cover how a throw works, the tricks that raise your odds, every Aniipod type and what it does, and how to save your best pods for the right targets. We will not repeat our beginner guide, our team building video or our evolution video, because this one is only about catching. A friendly warning as usual. Some numbers differ between guides and can change with patches, so the catch chance shown in your own game is the final word. By the end you will know exactly which pod to throw, and when to hold back.

sections.heading: How a throw works
sections.script: The basics are simple. You aim your crosshair at a wild Aniimo and throw an Aniipod. Here is the best part. Guides say you can hover the crosshair over the target to see the catch chance before you throw, so you never need to guess. If you miss, the Aniipod returns to you, so you can keep trying without losing it. The catch chance depends on several things, including the type of pod, the health of the target, whether it has been staggered, and even your position. Guides also mention that a target far above your level is harder to catch. Always check the percentage first, then decide which pod to use. It is a small habit, but it is the single most useful catching tip in the whole game, and it costs you nothing at all.

sections.heading: Sneak and back attacks
sections.script: Your first free boost is stealth. Guides agree that sleeping or unaware Aniimo are much easier to catch, and one guide even calls sleeping Aniimo practically free catches. So walk up slowly, stay out of sight and throw before the target notices you. Another tip is the back attack. Guides say a valid throw from behind gives a one point five times boost when you use the standard Aniipod outside of combat. So circle around, line up your shot from behind and throw. This is the cheapest way to catch common Aniimo, because you keep your stronger pods for later and you do not even have to fight first.

sections.heading: Weaken the target first
sections.script: If the Aniimo is awake and fighting, battle it first. Guides say that draining its health raises your chance, and so does filling its break gauge. A staggered Aniimo is far easier to catch than a fresh one. Some guides also list status effects, such as sleep and stun, as boosts to the catch chance, while a cloaked target is harder. The smart routine is to fight carefully, not to knock the target out too fast. Lower its health, break it, check the percentage with your crosshair and then throw. This costs a few seconds, but it can turn a poor chance into a safe one, and that saves precious pods.

sections.heading: The standard Aniipod line
sections.script: Now let us go through the pods. The basic Aniipod is the baseline, with one times the catch odds, and it is the one you will use most. The Aniipod Pro raises the chance to one point five times. The Aniipod Mega doubles the chance, and the Aniipod Hyper also doubles it, with a faster toss that helps against quick targets. The Aniipod Track doubles it as well, and it follows nearby targets, which helps when your aim is rough. Guides say you can get these from shops, quests, rank chests and events, and some from homeland production. Start with the plain Aniipod, and move up only when the displayed chance really needs it.

sections.heading: The Tumbler
sections.script: The Tumbler is the pod that many players ignore. It is a rolling pod, and one useful trait is that it can catch more than one Aniimo as it moves. Guides describe it as stronger in special situations. During Wild Surges and with Aniimo gathered through the Nurture system, its catch bonus becomes much larger. Guides disagree about the exact numbers, so we keep this rough, but they all agree that a Tumbler beats a basic pod in those moments. You can find it as a quest reward, from shops and from some event sources. If you plan to hunt a Wild Surge for rare spawns, stock up on Tumblers beforehand.

sections.heading: Ultra and Sparkling Cube
sections.script: Next come the premium pods. The Aniipod Ultra always captures its target, according to the guides we checked, though one guide treats this as less settled, so check your own game. Guides also say the caught Aniimo has at least Elite level potential. The Sparkling Cube is the top prize. It always captures, and it gives your Aniimo the Sparkling form with perfect potential. These pods are rare. Guides list sources such as Elite Training, special shops and the stamp and badge shops. Because they are so rare, do not waste them on common Aniimo. Keep them for rare spawns, strong targets and Sparkling hunts.

sections.heading: Which pod for which target
sections.script: Here is a simple plan. For common Aniimo, sneak up and throw a standard Aniipod from behind. For a target that is awake, weaken it, check the percentage, and use a Pro or a Mega only if the chance is low. For fast targets, the Hyper or the Track helps. For a Wild Surge, bring Tumblers. For rare spawns and the Aniimo you really want, use an Ultra or a Sparkling Cube. The rule is to always use the weakest pod that works. That way your stock of strong pods lasts for the moments that matter, instead of disappearing on easy targets that you could have caught for almost nothing. Think of your pods like a budget. Spend a little on the easy catches, and keep the big spending for the Aniimo that will define your team for many hours.

sections.heading: Finding your Aniimo
sections.script: One last piece is knowing where and when to look. Some Aniimo only appear at certain times or in certain weather, such as night, rain or snow, and the Aniilog shows these conditions. Guides say you can skip time to reach a night window, so you do not have to wait. Check the Aniilog for any Aniimo you are missing, and match your trip to its conditions. Then stock the right pods before you leave. A catching trip with a plan is much more efficient than random wandering, and it feeds your collection, your research and your team all at the same time.

sections.heading: Your catching checklist
sections.script: Here is your quick checklist. One, hover the crosshair and read the catch chance before every throw. Two, sneak up on sleeping or unaware Aniimo and throw from behind. Three, drain health and fill the break gauge on awake targets. Four, use the weakest pod that works. Five, keep Tumblers for Wild Surges. Six, save Ultra pods and Sparkling Cubes for rare targets and Sparkling hunts. Seven, check the Aniilog for weather and time conditions before a trip. Follow these steps and you will waste far fewer pods, and your collection will grow much faster than before. Save this video so you can check the list before your next trip.

sections.heading: What is your best catch
sections.script: That was our full guide to catching in Aniimo. Sneak, weaken, check the chance, and match the right Aniipod to the target. Which Aniipod do you use most, and what is the best Aniimo you have caught so far? Tell us in the comments, because we love reading your catches.
